sections.lever checks:
- Origin: caller (Claude Code, Opus 5.5), sketch i15 (notes/ideas.md, round 3, 2026-10-08), written after q02 and q03 were reported "too easy" at the form's quick test (notes/feedback-index.md r1-r2). Promoted directly; no sketch screen or model run.
- Snapshot: rev 0 prepared 2026-10-08, tested_sha256 7624ab15ae37b756eeda06dc5f3e7145bc32443cd51351371dcf746426069a2e (runs/q05-r0-v2-7624ab15ae37b756eeda06dc5f3e7145bc32443cd51351371dcf746426069a2e-platform; form fields and one corpus copy, no packets or model runs). Mechanical preflight and full hand-over run at this boundary; platform validation pending.
- Family and target: same series, right edition, chosen by publication date: the event is reported in the release that prints the next quarter-end figure, dated one day after the event, so the figure in that release was not yet published (the aq-00964 q01 shape, with a published measured figure in place of an outlook); difficulty_target medium (user: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Measured platform result: pending.
- Dependency plan: D08 L99 (launch January 15, 2026) and L13 (Doc 8 dated January 16, 2026) -> the 4Q25 figure was unpublished at launch; D07 L13 (dated October 17, 2025) and L77 ($401M at 3Q25 quarter-end) -> latest published figure; D10 L73 ($335M at 2Q26 quarter-end); D10 L367 ("backlog" = "to be installed"). (335 - 401) / 401 = -16.459% -> -16.5%.
- Universe: not applicable (two figures). Published backlog series for reference, one release each: year-end 2023 $270M (D01 endnote 8), 3Q24 $288M (D02), 4Q24 $346M (D03), 1Q25 $356M (D05), 2Q25 $444M (D06), 3Q25 $401M (D07), 4Q25 $320M (D08), 1Q26 $315M (D09), 2Q26 $335M (D10); no release repeats an earlier quarter's backlog.
- Necessity: D08 is the only document that names the Digital Asset Platform's launch and dates it (D10 L74 reports a separate Luxembourg tokenized fund servicing capability; D04 L19 lists "Digital Assets" only as a partnership area; D09 does not mention it). Without D08 the launch date, and so the figure, cannot be identified; a guessed launch between October 17, 2025 and January 16, 2026 would land on the gold (stated risk). D07 is the only source of the 3Q25 backlog ($401M); without it the latest pre-launch figure is missing (D08 gives only 4Q25's $320M and 4Q25 wins). D10 is the only source of the June 30, 2026 backlog ($335M); without it, D09's 1Q26 $315M as the end gives -21.4%.
- Selected-lever checks (python Decimal, 2026-10-08): Same series, right edition: taking Doc 8's own 4Q25 figure ($320M, published January 16, 2026, the release that reports the launch) gives (335 - 320) / 320 = +4.6875% (+4.7%), the opposite sign. Calculate across documents: start and end come from Doc 7 and Doc 10. Other routes: 1Q26 $315M as the end -21.4%; 2Q25 $444M as the start -24.5%. None gives -16.5%.
- Targeted failure modes: FM1 (Wrong year or edition, Uses the wrong period or date) recomputes +4.7% from D08 L85 ($320M) and D10 L73. Considered and not declared: AUC/A to be installed ($3.6 trillion to $2.9 trillion) and servicing fee revenue wins, which the question's "servicing fee revenue backlog" rules out.
- Calculation verification: python Decimal: 335 - 401 = -66; -66 / 401 = -0.16458853 -> -16.459% -> -16.5% (half-up and half-even agree; -16.46% at two decimals; 0.009 points from the -16.45 boundary, with exact whole-million inputs).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: grep "Digital Asset" and "tokeniz" across D01-D10 (hits D08 L86/L99, D10 L74/L79, D04 L19); "to be installed" figures as listed under Universe; the capture's overviews state no backlog figure; Doc 8's overview mentions "digital asset platform launches" among its strategic initiatives, with no date (capture line 85), which if anything supports the 4Q25 reading.
- Precision/readings: "latest figure it had published when it launched" fixes the start by publication date: Doc 8 (January 16, 2026) is after the January 15 launch, Doc 7 (October 17, 2025) before it, and no release falls between them. "Quarter-end servicing fee revenue backlog" is the releases' servicing fee revenue to be installed (D10 L367), not AUC/A to be installed. Whole-million inputs; one decimal.
- Completeness: no source gaps (capture complete, 10 of 10 documents read in full; doc-map coverage full).
- Style/set review: one ask; "backlog" paraphrases the releases' "to be installed" with their own alias. Set: q01 (AUM carve-out) and q04 (first-half expenses) use other metrics, documents and mechanisms; no question gives another's answer or path. All three use Doc 10 for their latest figure.
- Warnings answered: origin/export (origin: claude is accurate; the export tool takes origin user only, and the form's authorship statements are the user's to make); period (rule 9b heuristic on "quarter-end": the end is the date June 30, 2026, the start is fixed by the January 15, 2026 launch and the releases' publication dates, and State Street reports calendar quarters).

sections.question:
By what percentage did State Street's quarter-end servicing fee revenue backlog change from the latest
figure it had published when it launched its Digital Asset Platform to its figure for June 30, 2026?
Give the sign and round to one decimal place.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 8, 4Q25 highlights, note (b)): State Street's Digital Asset Platform was launched on January 15, 2026.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 8, dateline): Doc 8, the release that reports the launch, is dated January 16, 2026, the day after the launch, so the quarter-end figures it reports had not been published when the platform launched.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 7, dateline and 3Q25 highlights): the 3Q25 release, dated October 17, 2025, reported quarter-end servicing fee revenue of $401 million to be installed in future periods.

Step 4. Doc 7 and Doc 8: October 17, 2025 is before the January 15, 2026 launch, and no release in the bundle falls between Doc 7 and Doc 8, so $401 million was the latest such figure published when the platform launched.

Step 5. Source input (Doc 10, 2Q26 highlights): quarter-end servicing fee revenue to be installed in future periods was $335 million at the end of 2Q26 (June 30, 2026).

Step 6. Source input (Doc 10, In this news release): the releases call servicing fee revenue to be installed the "backlog".

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 7 and Doc 10): 335 - 401 = -66 ($ millions).

Step 8. Calculation (Doc 7, change as a share of the earlier figure): -66 / 401 = -16.5% (one decimal place).
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Wrong year or edition
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Doc 8 lists the Digital Asset Platform launch among its 4Q25 highlights, beside a
$320 million backlog, but dates the launch January 15, 2026, a day before its own release. The latest
published figure was 3Q25's $401 million (Doc 7): Doc 10's 335 against 401 is -16.5%, not +4.7%.
